audit.whatIsWrong: The page treats this as an even 'tricky' lane throughout. It is not: Orianna owns levels 1-5 outright and loses the game after two items, and the packet itself flags the contradiction — 45.02% win rate against a chart giving Orianna six of seven stages.
audit.why: Kit-grounded: Null Sphere reaches 650 against your 815, Force Pulse is 21s at rank 1 and must charge off nearby spellcasts, and Kassadin has no waveclear before Riftwalk — so the early lane is free. After that Void Stone reduces the magic damage that is your entire kit, Null Sphere shields magic damage on top, and Riftwalk drops to 2s at rank 3 with damage that grows per cast. Difficulty is a clock, not a constant.
audit.corrected: Chart, tldr, winCon, early/mid/late and spikes now say the same thing: free before 6, decided by two items.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json (P text, Q range 650/cd 9, E cd 21/20/19/18/17, R cd 5/3.5/2)

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes claimed 'Luden's makes Q-W a third of a health bar' — a magnitude with no source — and named level 6 as your spike when level 6 is his.
audit.why: Riftwalk at 6 is his relief window; the page had it as your doubling. And the kit gives no damage numbers to support a fraction.
audit.corrected: Spikes restated as: Lost Chapter funds the shove, 6 is his relief, Luden's keeps you ahead of his scaling.

audit.whatIsWrong: None of the decisive interactions were stated. Nothing on the page mentioned Void Stone reducing magic damage, Null Sphere granting a magic-damage shield, Riftwalk's per-cast mana escalation, or Force Pulse needing to charge.
audit.why: Void Stone plus the Null Sphere shield is why your damage underperforms against him specifically; Riftwalk's escalating mana cost is the actual resource you track rather than a cooldown that is 2 seconds; and Force Pulse being uncharged is why the early step-ups are safe.
audit.corrected: All four now appear across breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.late, report[5], report[8] and the do's/don'ts.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json (P, Q shield flag, E charge text, R mana text)

audit.why: 45.02% over 864 games, matching the brief's games field. This is the number the corrected chart now agrees with.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (catalogue defect 3), and dosFull[2].d invented a 'fifteen-second invitation' for an ability that is 5s at rank 1 and 2s at rank 3.
audit.why: The invented fifteen seconds would get a reader killed; it is off by an order of magnitude at rank 3.
audit.corrected: Real numbers throughout; the Riftwalk window restated as a mana cost rather than a cooldown, which is what actually limits it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The brief flags Nether Blade as an auto-attack reset and the page never mentioned it; dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were the tradeGood/tradeBad strings pasted under unrelated titles (catalogue defect 2).
audit.why: The reset is the burst tell — the wind-up, not a cast bar, is what you react to.
audit.corrected: Nether Blade's reset now stated in dontsFull[2].d; both pasted bodies replaced with content answering their own titles.

audit.whatIsWrong: The wave section was the generic Orianna paragraph and described the worst wave as a freeze at his tower — the opposite of the truth here.

notes: Chart: the packet's own defect line called this out — 45.02% win rate against a chart giving Orianna six of seven stages. I resolved it in the direction the kits support rather than by splitting the difference. Rows 0-4 go to Orianna in both layers (win[0..4] already read Orianna; only phases[].side needed moving), row 5 goes to Skill in both (win[5] already Skill), and row 6 flips to Kassadin — phases[6].side already read Kassadin, so I moved win[6] to match and rewrote phases[6].why and content whys[6] in the same proposal so the row and its sentence argue the same case. Grounds for giving him 2+ items: Void Stone reduces magic damage and Orianna is entirely magic, Null Sphere adds a magic-damage shield on top, and Riftwalk at 2s beats a 410-range Shockwave. phases[].rating (5,5,5,5,6,7,7) already rises late and needed no change — it now agrees with the corrected chart. content whys[5] also had a label bug: it described the Level 6 window while sitting in the First item row; rewritten to the row it is in. Kassadin is male, so no pronoun corrections were needed here — unlike the other matchups in this slice.
